locator.section: Chapter 4 Basic Mechanisms of Ion Fragmentation; radical-site (alpha) cleavage of amines

evidence.curator_note: ARC COUNT / DRAWN-vs-INFERRED (convention D): Figure 4.4 is the diethylamine BAR SPECTRUM annotated with wavy cleavage-marks (which bond breaks -> which m/z) and the '58a' peak label; it draws 0 curved electron-pushing arrows. The 3-fishhook alpha-cleavage flow encoded here is curator-inferred from the book's own alpha attribution (the cleavage-mark + 'a' label), not transcribed from drawn arcs. Concrete example: diethylamine molecular ion, n-ionized at nitrogen, CH3CH2-N(+.)(H)-CH2CH3 (m/z 73, M+.). The alpha (Ca-Cb) bond cleaves with loss of .CH3 to give the iminium ion CH2=N(+)(H)-CH2CH3 at m/z 58, the base peak (labelled '58a' on the spectrum). Book draws 0 curved arrows for this step: the mechanism is shown by a squiggly bond-cleavage mark drawn across the CH3-C(alpha) bond with the retained-fragment mass '58' bracketed beneath it (McLafferty's cleavage notation, not electron-pushing arrows). All 3 electron moves are encoded here for electron balance (odd electron on N into the forming N=C pi bond; one electron of the breaking Ca-Cb sigma into that pi bond; the second electron of that sigma onto the departing methyl); NONE is drawn as an arc on the page.

Cross-linked MØD rule IMS_4_43_ (book eq 4.43, authored as 'displacement reaction' in the German-edition provenance). VERIFIED against this scheme: its DFS left pattern [C]1(H)(H)(H)[C]5(H)(H)[N+.]8(H)[C]10(H)(H)[C]13(H)(H)(H) is atom-for-atom the diethylamine radical cation used here, and its right side [C]1[C]5[N+]8(H){=}[C]10(H)(H) . [C.]13(H)(H)(H) is exactly the encoded step: it cleaves the Ca-Cb bond (C10-C13), forms the N8=C10 pi bond incident to the pi-forming alpha carbon, and migrates the radical from N to the departing methyl. The rule parses in the container to 1 left / 2 right components, consistent with a single fragmentation. Because diethylamine is symmetric the rule's C10/C13 correspond to either ethyl group. No mismatch: cleaved bond IS incident to the double-bond-forming atom.
m/z 58 is the base peak of the diethylamine spectrum (Figure 4.4), explicitly labelled '58a' (alpha cleavage).
